s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass measured 12 cm and was non-tender
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Noted the lesion two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
Denied pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Medical history notable for hypertension and hysterectomy in 2016
Post-menopausal with no history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam was unremarkable
Pelvic exam was otherwise normal
Routine laboratory results were within normal limits

differentials: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck

shortlist.label: Canal of Nuck hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the leading preoperative impression and ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Vulvar lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign tumor that could present as a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could cause a gradual enlargement of a vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that could present as a large, painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that could cause a gradual enlargement of a vulvar mass, although less likely given the absence of pain or other symptoms

shortlist.label: Vulvar fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could present as a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Superficial angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could cause a gradual enlargement of a vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Vulvar sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that could present as a large, painless vulvar mass, although less likely given the absence of pain or other symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, gradually enlarging vulvar mass extending into the inguinal region, along with ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal, is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, which is a rare hernia that occurs when tissue protrudes through a weak spot in the abdominal wall near the inguinal canal.

rejected.label: Vulvar lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically mobile and not fixed to surrounding structures, unlike the mass described in the patient.

rejected.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are usually painful and may cause urinary symptoms, which the patient denied.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: Aggressive angiomyxomas are rare, locally invasive tumors that often cause pain and tenderness, not consistent with the patient's painless presentation.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: Bartholin gland carcinomas are typically painful and may cause bleeding or discharge, which the patient did not experience.

rejected.label: Vulvar fibroma
rejected.why: Fibromas are usually small, firm, and mobile, unlike the large, gradually enlarging mass described in the patient.

rejected.label: Superficial angiomyxoma
rejected.why: Superficial angiomyxomas are rare, benign tumors that may cause local invasion, but the patient's presentation and ultrasound findings are more consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia.

rejected.label: Vulvar sarcoma
rejected.why: Vulvar sarcomas are rare, malignant tumors that often cause pain, bleeding, or other symptoms, which the patient did not experience.
